identity.basis: The registry target is Dutch-taught, and the adopted 2026–27 OER names Media en Journalistiek as the only current Dutch-taught specialization. The two English routes and closed teach-out routes do not match this target; the selection follows formal target identity, not UCR fit.

formalSource.finding: OER Article9.1 requires Discourse Analysis before Discourse and Social Interaction; all B1/B2 must pass for thesis/colloquium. The Dutch route table omits that prerequisite. Individual exemption under3.7 is not a cohort waiver.

contentFindings.formuleren: Standardized written/spoken discourse analysis, registers and formulation effects; this content similarity supplies no formal equivalence.
contentFindings.discourse: Inductive conversation analysis of natural and institutional talk, turns and social action; exam55/research45. No full UCR counterpart is claimed.
contentFindings.newsText: Independent/group journalistic articles, newsworthiness, verification, sources, interviews, editorial peerfeedback; practical70/theory30. Broader nonfiction writing is not a replacement.
contentFindings.newsImage: Journalistic reel, reportage and explainer; footage/interviews/editing and media-image theory. UCR documentary is a genuine but narrower/differently framed contribution.
contentFindings.dataJournalism: Finding/cleaning/analyzing/visualizing data and an individual newsworthy story; group50/final50. UCR R work contributes methods, not the full editorial product.
contentFindings.narrativity: News narrative, truth claims, ethnographic content analysis and membership categorization; text-film adaptation supplies only a bounded cross-media narrative relationship.
contentFindings.visualRhetoric: Visual/verbal cognitive processing, advertising metaphors and instructional images; generic visual analysis is insufficient for a direct match.
contentFindings.commissionedResearch: Actual empirical research responding to media/journalism organizations; may require new methods; no guaranteed UCR commission.
contentFindings.thesis: 9EC individual supervised thesis with workplan, GO/STOP and independent second reading; 3EC symposium/public-science colloquium. All B1/B2 must pass.
contentFindings.future: Public recruitment page marks 2027–2028 and2028–2029 lists provisional. No future substitution or 2026 cohort bridge is certified.

boundary: The documented 2026–2027 Media and Journalism allocation totals 180 EC, including 30 EC of approved open study. This is a qualified comparison of that published academic content, not a certified progression route for 2026 entrants. Discourse and Social Interaction requires Discourse Analysis, which is absent from the route allocation. The applicable prerequisite, any extra credit or replacement, and consequent thesis access remain unverified. Future 2027–2028 and 2028–2029 recruitment revisions are provisional and are not substituted into this comparison.

uncertainties.fact: The adopted OER and current annual Discourse and Social Interaction page require passing Discourse Analysis, absent from the Dutch route table. The thesis and colloquium require all first- and second-year courses. Future recruitment revisions are provisional, with no adopted replacement/credit bridge.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Discourse Analysis is an additional compulsory course whose credits displace open study or another allocation, or a different preparatory course is formally imposed.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The allocation and unrestricted elective capacity are not certified. More specialized discourse preparation may increase the already explicit specialist gap. The published media, language, journalism and empirical subjects and the actual broader UCR response remain independently supported; no exact conversation-analysis or full-degree equivalence is claimed.

adverseResolutions.resolution: An authoritative cohort-wide equivalence, waiver or corrected prerequisite permits the published sequence.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: No waiver is assumed. It would resolve access without changing the confirmed current subject/method content or the broader, explicitly limited UCR response.

adverseResolutions.resolution: An adopted revised cohort removes the disputed course and introduces distinct innovation, deception or social-media methods, changing advanced weighting and thesis preparation.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Those future changes and a complete 2026-entry progression are excluded from this current 2026–2027 content comparison. No claim is made that the current allocation predicts that future route. The demonstrated response to the currently documented media/narrative, journalism, public-information and research content remains valid within the stated boundary.

exhaustedResearch: No repeat broad search for a waiver. Primary source HTTP retrieval succeeded despite web-reader errors; those access errors are not evidence of academic absence. No contact or outreach.
